title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring containing no repeated characters.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the maximum length.
constraints: s may contain letters, digits, spaces, and symbols

examples.explanation: The longest valid substring is abc.
The longest valid substring is b.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Group strings that are anagrams of one another. Sort strings inside each group and sort the groups lexicographically by their first element.
inputFormat: Next n lines: one string per line
outputFormat: Print the number of groups, followed by one space-separated group per line.

examples.input:
6
eat
tea
tan
ate
nat
bat
examples.output:
3
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan
examples.explanation: Strings with identical character counts belong together.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest palindromic substring. If multiple answers have the same length, return the leftmost one.

examples.explanation: bab and aba are valid, but bab appears first.

title: Decode String
description: Decode an encoded string where k[encoded_text] means encoded_text is repeated k times. Encodings may be nested.
inputFormat: One line containing the encoded string

examples.explanation: a is repeated three times and bc twice.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Find the shortest substring of s containing every character of t with the required frequency. Return an empty string if no such window exists.
outputFormat: Print the minimum valid window, or an empty line.

examples.explanation: BANC is the shortest substring containing A, B, and C.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Implement full-string matching for a pattern containing '.' and '*'. Dot matches any single character; star matches zero or more of the preceding element.

examples.explanation: The pattern matches only one character.

title: Wildcard Matching
description: Implement full-string wildcard matching where '?' matches one character and '*' matches any sequence, including the empty sequence.

examples.explanation: Star can match the whole string.

title: Edit Distance
description: Return the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to transform word1 into word2.

title: Text Justification
description: Format words into lines of exactly maxWidth characters. Fully justify all lines except the last, which must be left-justified.
inputFormat: First line: integers n and maxWidth
Next n lines: one word per line
outputFormat: Print each justified line between pipe characters so spaces remain visible.
